messages.content: hey ome can we test our internal capabilitites please, will you list them for me and we run through each one

Yeah mate — we can absolutely do that.

First up, I can list the capability groups we’ve got wired in (Browser / Hud / Chat / Config), then we’ll go one by one and do a quick sanity test on each (like open a tab, scroll, HUD message, chat ops, config read, etc).

I’ll pull the full list now.  
{"cap": "ListCapabilities"}
read this page and let me know if htere are any take aways to focus on to make you better as a web assistant
ok maybe can you ask chat gbt to provide a summary for you by giving a nice little prompt
do you think we can control the size of our system prompt as its being passed with every call

Yeah mate — and you *should*, because if you’re passing the whole system prompt every call you’re burning latency + tokens for no good reason.

Two cases:

## 1) ChatGPT/OpenAI “preferred mode” (best)
You **don’t pass the big system prompt every call**.
- Put the big rulebook into a **stored Prompt** (server-side) *once*
- Then each call only sends: `page.md + last_action + task`
Result: tiny payloads, fast calls.

So here the “size control” is basically: **make the per-call input small**, and keep the rulebook out of the loop.

## 2) Everyone else / local LLM fallback (you *are* passing it every call)
Then yes, you need hard controls, otherwise it’ll feel like mud:
- **Split the rulebook**:
  - `rules_tiny.txt` (core contract + output schema + a few examples)
  - `rules_full.txt` (big library, only use when needed)
- **Send only what’s relevant**:
  - Don’t send 300 capabilities, send a filtered subset based on the task (eg “navigation”, “scrolling”, “tabs”, etc.)
- **Cap the page snapshot**:
  - DOM summary not full DOM
  - top-N visible interactables
  - compress text, drop duplicates
- **Keep history local** and only send last 1–3 events (not the whole novel)

## Quick check: which mode are you currently running?
- Are you calling OpenAI with a `prompt_id` (stored Prompt), or are you still doing “system prompt + page.md” every request?

If you paste your current call code (the bit in `LLMClient` / `ws_server.py`), I’ll tell you exactly where to cut it down and what to move into the stored Prompt vs per-call input.
